record.original_question: In the same decision-stump setting where X = [0, 1]^n, H_b is the midpoint-rule stump class induced by the dataset, E_b is the effective stump set obtained after removing dominated stumps, and U_b^T = union_{t=1}^T {h_t} is the set of unique decision stumps selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_b during T rounds, is it true that for mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D sampled from P, there exist m_0, T_0 > 0 such that whenever m > m_0 and T > T_0, the conditional expectation E[|U_b^T| | D] is bounded above by (log T + 1)^c for some c in [1, 2), P-almost surely?

evidence.quote: Further, denote by U_b^T equiv union_{t=1}^T {h_t} the set of unique decision stumps actually selected by Optimal AdaBoost from E_b after T rounds.

Conjecture 4 (Logarithmic Growth on Unique Stumps) For mu-almost all probability spaces (D, Sigma, P) and any dataset D ~ P, there exist m0, T0 > 0, such that if m > m0 and T > T0, we have E[ |U_b^T| | D ] <= (log T + 1)^c, for some c in [1, 2), P-almost surely.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let the input space be $X = [0,1]^n$ and the label space $Y = \{-1, +1\}$. Fix a probability space $(D, \Sigma, P)$ on $X \times Y$, where $D$ varies over a measurable family endowed with a probability measure $\mu$ on the space of such distributions. A dataset $\mathcal{D} = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^m$ is drawn i.i.d. from $P$.

Decision stumps. For each coordinate $j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$, sort the values $\{x_{i,j}\}_{i=1}^m$ and let the candidate thresholds be the midpoints between consecutive sorted values. The midpoint-rule stump class $H_b$ consists of all classifiers of the form $h(x) = s\cdot \mathrm{sign}(x_j - \theta)$ where $j$ is a coordinate, $\theta$ is one of these midpoint thresholds, and $s \in \{-1,+1\}$. The effective stump set $E_b \subseteq H_b$ is obtained from $H_b$ by removing dominated stumps (i.e., stumps that produce the same labeling on $\mathcal{D}$ as another stump and are eliminated under the standard equivalence/domination reduction).

Optimal AdaBoost. Run Optimal AdaBoost on $\mathcal{D}$ with weak-learner output drawn from $E_b$: at each round $t = 1, 2, \dots, T$, the weak learner returns a stump $h_t \in E_b$ minimizing the weighted training error under the current distribution. Define
$$U_b^T \;=\; \bigcup_{t=1}^{T} \{h_t\},$$
the set of unique stumps selected during the first $T$ rounds.

Question. Prove or disprove: for $\mu$-almost every probability space $(D, \Sigma, P)$ and any dataset $\mathcal{D}$ sampled from $P$, there exist $m_0, T_0 > 0$ and an exponent $c \in [1, 2)$ such that whenever $m > m_0$ and $T > T_0$,
$$\mathbb{E}\!\left[\,|U_b^T|\;\middle|\;\mathcal{D}\,\right] \;\le\; (\log T + 1)^c,$$
$P$-almost surely.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture was posed as an open problem about the logarithmic growth of the number of unique decision stumps selected by Optimal AdaBoost. A subsequent overview notes that Belanich and Ortiz studied the ergodic dynamics of AdaBoost and obtained related intermediate results, but no source found explicitly resolves this specific conjectural bound $(\log T + 1)^c$ with $c \in [1,2)$. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in Optimal AdaBoost and Decision Stumps
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems including conjecture on logarithmic growth of unique stumps.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Overview of AdaBoost: Reconciling its views
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ergodic dynamics results by Belanich and Ortiz related to AdaBoost on decision stumps.
status_evidence.claim: Related results have been obtained but the specific logarithmic-growth conjecture is not reported as resolved.
